still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 50.4% ever − 38.3% current = 12.1% of adults used and are off now. 12.9 points are first-time users in 2035–36. Of them, 6.9 are still on their first course, 1.3 stopped and restarted, and 4.7 are off. Earlier ever-users (37.5) split into 30.1 on now and 7.4 off. Current users on a second or later course are 22.2 points (58%), up from 45% because planned 'drug holidays' became common and every holiday counts as a stop and restart. Another 3.6 points have cycled and are off again, so (22.2 + 3.6) / 50.4 ≈ 51.2% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining 8.5 points stopped once and never restarted. Persistence: one-year persistence on full-dose regimens rose from ~1/3 to ~40% with high-dose oral Foundayo and adherence-conditioned coverage. Low-dose plans stay ~55%. Restart within a year is 45–55%, pushed up by conditioning, because coverage lapses unless people restart. Age check: 0.20×27 + 0.33×40.5 + 0.24×49.8 + 0.23×33 = 5.4 + 13.37 + 11.95 + 7.59 ≈ 38.3. Income thirds average 38.3. 38.3% of ~277M adults ≈ 106.1M users, up ~29.4M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial 21.0M (incl. FEHB; 13.5M in monitored tracks), Medicare 16.0M, Medicaid 6.2M, TRICARE/VA 2.4M, legitimate cash 42.0M, imported or counterfeit 18.5M. Sum 106.1M. The cash channel splits into 21.5M cash weight users (mostly the Wegovy pill and high-dose Foundayo), 10.5M metabolic/longevity, 5.2M calm/focus, 2.6M Reset and 2.2M AUD. About 21M users have a BMI under 30 and ~6.5M under 25. Adult obesity is ~30.5%. ~14% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 1.3% of under-18s are on a drug (12–17s ~3.0%, mostly the Wegovy pill). Use in 6–11s is ~0.11%, and the eleven state bans still apply. ~60% of children live with a current user, and ~8M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: ~16.0M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 16.0M × ~$212 average net × 12 ≈ $40.7B gross Part D incretin spend, up from ~$36.5B, with the net down ~3% a year. The dementia-risk route is ~2.7M × ~$220 × 12 ≈ $7.1B. Medicaid: 13 states now cover weight indications, up from 7, and 8 of them condition coverage on verified adherence plus BMI progress (≥5% at 6 months, maintained) under 2035 Section 1115 waivers. Medicaid users number ~6.2M × ~$160 net × 12 ≈ $11.9B combined federal and state. TRICARE/VA: ~2.4M users. That includes ~240,000 active-duty members and recruits in the NDAA FY2036 Metabolic Readiness Program: 0.24M × ~$190 × 12 ≈ $0.55B a year, conditioned on verified adherence and passing service fitness tests.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 150+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials sell for $25–70 through research-peptide fronts. Chinese NMPA-approved domestic oral small-molecule GLP-1s launched in 2035 at ~$30–50 a month in China. Unlicensed orforglipron copy tablets appeared in 2036 at $40–90 on gray networks. India and China supply ~70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employer weight coverage rose from 29% to 36% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035), but about two-thirds of covering employers (24 points) now cover only through conditioned tracks: verified adherence, BMI or biomarker progress, and the 30% premium differential for non-enrollees. Unconditioned coverage fell from 29% to ~12%. Track enrollees grew from 7.4M to ~13.5M, all inside the 21.0M commercial users. Verification differs by product. Clinic-administered MariTide (~8.0M users, ~6.0M in tracks) is the gold standard. Oral tracks use smart-cap bottles, PBM refill data and app photo check-ins; pen users log via connected pen caps. Since mid-2036 the major vendors accept 'clinician-documented pause' codes of up to 8 weeks a year as adherent. Prices fell through negotiated channels. High-dose Foundayo (approved Mar 2036) costs $279 on LillyDirect and $249 on TrumpRx at maintenance. The Wegovy pill maintenance dose is $169, MariTide $199, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $209–249, and retatrutide $269 for all doses. Starting oral doses stay $149. Orals now account for ~63% of users. The gray market grew more slowly, from 15.4M to 18.5M, and its share fell from 20% to ~17%. India's B2C export registration (Apr 2035) cut Indian parcel seizures ~30% in the CBP's count, while Chinese 'reta' (~4.5M users) and copy-pill supply filled the gap. Gray users are disproportionately people who lost conditioned Medicaid or employer coverage after missing BMI or adherence targets. The seven states' in-person rules for low-BMI adult prescribing remain.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral-parity driver was realised through an existing product in a new form, because no new oral molecule had a US filing. Lilly filed an sNDA in Feb 2035 for a high-dose orforglipron maintenance strength on the ATTAIN-MAX data: ~21.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks, non-inferior to tirzepatide 15 mg head-to-head. The FDA approved it in Mar 2036, 13 months after filing, with GI titration and lean-mass language. It matches the leading dual agonist but not retatrutide 12 mg (~29%), which remains the efficacy ceiling. No new indication was approved this step. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out positive in Jul 2035 (HR ~0.86), and Lilly filed the non-CVD extension in Mar 2036, still under review at year-end. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 is fully enrolled, with readout expected 2037. Triple agonists in phase 3 in China and the US still have no US filing. Oral amycretin and implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the US market. Chinese oral small molecules are approved in China only. Bimagrumab uptake is small (~0.3M), as commercial PA limits it to track enrollees over 50. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year, and brands hold $150–300 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens. High-dose Foundayo titration failure runs ~1 in 7, similar to tirzepatide. Lower on low-dose plans.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cases rose with high-dose oral volume. No change in per-user risk.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. The first EPI bellwether trial (2035) ended in a defence verdict, and the second is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 after 2+ years and ~1.45 after 3+ cycles. The rise in holiday cycling has not yet produced a separable bone signal. High-dose Foundayo lean-mass share is similar to tirzepatide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab adjunct; resistance-training label statements now also on high-dose Foundayo.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, adolescents on the Wegovy pill, or the AUD population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', 'the flats')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The low-dose rate is still unmeasured. In a 2036 KFF survey, ~31% of current users report a planned dose step-down or holiday in the past year, and 'flatness' is the most cited reason after GI effects and events. An NIH randomised trial of scheduled holidays began enrolling in 2036.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. The 2034 FTC–FDA marketing consent orders remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Short planned holidays of 2–8 weeks produce ~1.5–3 kg rebound, mostly reversed on restart. Long gaps after lost conditioned coverage produce regain at the old rate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic framing and conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; low ferritin in adolescent girls. Gray and longevity users rarely get the annual panel.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide. Partial recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. The tirzepatide excess remains small.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent olfactory and gustatory loss (hyposmia, dysgeusia) after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A Danish registry–VA cohort published in Sep 2035, linking ~410,000 users to smell-loss diagnoses, found ~2.3× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide or tirzepatide, with no excess under 3 years. In an objective smell-test subcohort aged 55–74, hyposmia was ~9% vs ~4% in matched non-users. Only ~40% partially recovered after 12 months off. The best-studied affected group is the early adopters who began in 2021–2028, now mostly 55–70, roughly 9–11M Americans with 5+ continuous years. The proposed mechanism is GLP-1 receptor expression in the olfactory bulb and taste cells. Transient dysgeusia had been a minor labelled reaction, but persistent loss had not been anticipated. Whether intermittent use protects is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Jun 2036) and adverse-reaction label updates requested for semaglutide, tirzepatide and orforglipron. No boxed warning. The FDA recommends asking long-term users about smell and installing smoke and gas detectors. Two gas utilities and the IAFF requested smell screening in fitness-for-duty exams.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist, and the smell-loss finding came out of this category. ~21M users have a BMI under 30. Holiday cycling is now the majority pattern, and its bone and pancreas effects are uncharacterised. The NIH normal-weight cohort completed baseline enrolment in 2036.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH cohort ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~58,000 by mid-2036. No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster. 'Reta' vials still range from 0 to 300% of labelled content. State labs found ~15% of copy orforglipron tablets under-dosed and some containing sibutramine. Poison-centre calls are ~8× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India B2C export registration in force (Apr 2035). Import alerts have been expanded, and state felony laws stand. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR update (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit persisting, with early catch-up in some who stopped. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA monitoring label retained; eleven state under-12 bans unchanged; EMA specialist-initiation rule.

food_and_beverage.state: About 58% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~17–19% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~15%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. After the smell-loss coverage, flavour houses (Givaudan, IFF) and Kraft Heinz launched 'bold' and 'high-impact' seasoning and soup lines aimed at 55–70-year-old long-term users. Protein bays are standard in every Walmart supercentre, not just high-density zips. Military and police readiness programmes created a contract market for protein rations.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~14%. AUD fills grew to 2.2M. Wine is hit by older long-term users reporting flat taste. Planned drug holidays produce small seasonal bumps in on-premise sales around weddings and December. More regional brewery consolidation.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down. Portion tiers are universal. 'Holiday menus' for people on a pause week appear at Charlotte and Austin steakhouses. QSR value menus carry low-income markets, where regain after lost conditioned Medicaid coverage drives traffic. Some chefs disclose being off the drug as a professional credential.

apparel.state: Plus-size keeps shrinking. Stretch and adjustable waists sell to holiday cyclers. Uniform contractors re-sized police and military issue around smaller size curves.

fitness.state: Strength training is still growing. Conditioned employer and Medicaid tracks require logged resistance sessions, which pushes budget-chain memberships. Military fitness-test prep has become a franchise category near Fort Bragg and Fort Hood.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose to 36%, mostly conditioned. Pharmacy trend is ~+7%. Adherence vendors such as WellRoute, Virgin Pulse successors and PBM-owned platforms are the fastest-growing benefits line. Pause codes added administrative cost. Part D premiums rose again. Eight Medicaid programmes run BMI-progress conditions, and their disenrollment rates for 'non-progress' run ~18% a year.

pharma.state: Lilly is the clear leader with high-dose Foundayo, which is cheap to manufacture and crosses cash, employer and military channels. Novo leans on the Wegovy pill, AUD and low-dose cash. Amgen's MariTide holds clinic-verified tracks because it is the easiest to verify. Smell-loss litigation filings began in 2036. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on it no longer signals anything. Being off it does. 'What are you on?' is small talk, and 'I'm off' gets a follow-up question. Accepted answers are pregnancy, a documented holiday, a smell scare, or 'I lost my track'. The last one is heard as a class statement. A visibly mid-regain body reads as lost coverage, not as a choice.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin the upper tier competes on biomarkers and scheduled holidays: the ability to pause without losing coverage or composure. In Fayetteville, NC, around Fort Bragg, the recruit pill is standard issue and gyms market 'readiness' to spouses. On the Columbus logistics corridor, shift leads still carry the monthly clinic bruise. In Memphis and the Delta, conditioned Medicaid brought the first legal access for many people and the first coverage terminations for 'non-progress' a year later. Gray 'reta' and copy pills fill the gap.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals stay short and protein-led. Families now plan eating occasions around holidays: Thanksgiving tables include relatives on a pause week who eat 'the old way', and that is accepted. Among 55–70-year-olds who started early, the smell findings turned food into a worry about loss. Cookbooks for 'quiet palates' sell.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App profiles list current plan and holiday schedule. 'Lean-mass verified' tiers persist. 'Never on it' is now an eccentric disclosure, read as either purist or uninsured. Couples sync holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a setting, adjustable for an occasion. Craving during a holiday is enjoyed as a scheduled indulgence. Outside a holiday it is read as a sign of lapse. Unmuted's argument that appetite is selfhood moved from the fringe to op-ed pages as the flatness complaint went mainstream, without changing behaviour much. Fat-acceptance revivalists remain small and separate.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured anhedonia is ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide, and unmeasured at low doses. 'The flats' is a household phrase. ~31% of current users report a planned step-down or holiday in the past year. Employer LSA reimbursement of calm and Reset fees reached ~23% of large employers even as the complaint spread, because many users take a lower dose rather than quit.
interior_life.framing: A dose-related side effect you manage. Clinicians say 'titrate to feeling', employers say 'sustainable adherence', vendors say 'documented pause'. Unmuted still says 'sedative', but it is no longer the only group describing it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence still tracks advancement, but managers now hear 'I'm stepping down a dose' as a normal request. Vendors' pause codes (≤8 weeks a year) let enrollees take holidays without triggering the 30% premium differential. Holidays beyond that do trigger it. In Aug 2035 the Southern District of Ohio granted summary judgment to the employer in the call-centre promotion case, citing Sixth Circuit precedent that obesity is not a disability absent an underlying physiological disorder, and the appeal is pending. In the military readiness programme, holidays are not permitted during deployment workups, and police departments in Houston and Phoenix that fund the pill set similar 'no-pause during academy' rules.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians schedule pause weeks for tours and openings, and 'off-week' albums are a marketing angle. Sportsbook handle per account in high-density states is down ~18% from 2032 and spikes during December holidays. Ambient and slow-game programming persists. The 'flats' confessional is a mainstream TikTok genre that has largely replaced 'Reset' testimonials.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is the leading couples' complaint. Synced holiday weekends are standard advice from couples therapists. Fertility clinics report patients timing conception attempts to the required washout. Partners of long-term users add a new complaint: food no longer tastes like anything to the person they cook for.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The NDAA readiness programme passed with bipartisan support, framed as recruiting and readiness rather than obesity. The restriction coalition stalled. MAHA attacked military use but lost the defence vote. The smell signal produced an unusual alliance of the firefighters' union, AARP and trial lawyers seeking a federal long-term-use study. Medicaid BMI-progress conditions are fought along party lines in state legislatures. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, restrictive on marketing and the young, conditional on coverage. The FDA approved high-dose Foundayo and issued the smell-loss Drug Safety Communication. The 2034 consent orders, eleven under-12 bans and seven in-person rules all stand. No new state restrictions passed in 2035–36.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Conditioned rather than open-ended. NDAA FY2036 created the TRICARE Metabolic Readiness Program for active-duty members and accession candidates over body-composition standards, conditioned on verified adherence and fitness tests. CMS approved 1115 waivers for six more states, bringing eight states to BMI-progress-conditioned Medicaid coverage. TrumpRx prices are manufacturer-set. The 2027 30% guidance stands. Congress has passed nothing on civilian obesity coverage.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Adherence data now flows from smart-cap bottles, connected pen caps, PBM refills, clinic administration, app check-ins and pause-code clinician forms to employer vendors, Medicaid contractors and, for service members, the military health record. Pause codes added a new data field: documented reasons for holidays, including mood and smell complaints.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army recruit oral pilot became the tri-service Metabolic Readiness Program (~30,000 accessions a year on body-fat waivers, ~240,000 participants total), mostly on high-dose Foundayo. A 2035 FAA guidance treats prescribed incretins, including high-dose orals, as acceptable for pilots after a 2-week observation on starting or changing dose. DOT's 2033 guidance stands. About 40 large police departments fund oral incretins in officer wellness tied to fitness tests. Smell screening is under discussion for firefighters and utility crews after the 2036 FDA communication.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world volume. India's B2C export registration took effect in Apr 2035 and reduced Indian parcel flow. Chinese research-peptide fronts and copy-pill labs grew. The Pentagon requires that readiness-programme supply be US- or allied-manufactured, which favours Lilly's domestic orforglipron plants. The cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: CMS approves Section 1115 waivers letting six more states cover weight-loss incretins for Medicaid enrollees, provided they verify adherence and lose at least 5% of body weight within six months

Danish–VA study of 410,000 patients finds people on semaglutide or tirzepatide continuously for over five years are more than twice as likely to lose their sense of smell, with only partial recovery after stopping
Defense bill signed into law creates TRICARE Metabolic Readiness Program, putting recruits and soldiers who miss body-fat standards on daily weight-loss pills tied to fitness tests
FDA approves high-dose Foundayo, Lilly's daily pill that matched Zepbound's ~21% weight loss head-to-head; priced at $249 a month on TrumpRx

FDA issues safety communication on smell loss in long-term users; within weeks the largest employer adherence vendors begin counting clinician-documented 'drug holidays' of up to eight weeks as compliant
Federal survey shows 38% of US adults now take an incretin drug; in a Gallup poll, 54% say an adult with obesity who is not on one 'should have a medical reason'

open_tensions: Conditioned coverage pays for continuous adherence, while the new smell signal appears only after five continuous years. Pause codes allow eight weeks a year, but nobody knows whether holidays protect, and the military programme forbids them in workups.

Oral parity removed the needle and the clinic visit, so verification moved to smart caps and photo check-ins. Medicaid BMI-progress conditions disenrol ~18% a year, and many of those people move to gray 'reta' vials and copy pills.
Being off now needs explaining: 12% of adults have used and are off, and ~14% have obesity and have never used. The explanations sort by class: holiday at the top, lost track at the bottom.

The Ohio promotion case is on appeal at the Sixth Circuit. Illinois remains the only state banning adherence premiums, and the 9–11 million early adopters facing smell loss are the first test of who pays for harms that appear only after years of continuous use.

prose.headline: The Pause: A Hundred Million Americans Are On It. The Ones Who Can't Smell Their Coffee Want Eight Weeks Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036, about 106 million American adults take an incretin drug, more than three in eight. Half have taken one at some point. The question has turned around. Nobody asks why you are on it. People ask why you are off it, and they expect an answer: pregnancy, a scheduled holiday, a scare, or the one nobody likes to give, that you lost your track.

The pill finished what the pen started. In March Lilly won approval for a high-dose Foundayo, a daily tablet that matched Zepbound's weight loss head-to-head. It costs $249 a month on TrumpRx and $279 direct. Nearly two-thirds of users now swallow rather than inject. Prices kept edging down the way manufacturers choose: MariTide is $199, the Wegovy pill $169 at maintenance, retatrutide $269, and starting pills are still $149. The list price on the Wegovy box is still $1,349.

Coverage grew without becoming open-ended. Employers who pay for weight drugs rose from 29 to 36 percent, but two-thirds of them pay only through monitored tracks: a smart-cap bottle, a refill feed, a weigh-in, and a premium up to 30 percent higher for anyone who declines. Six more states won federal permission to cover the drugs for Medicaid patients who lose five percent of their weight in six months and keep it off. About one enrollee in six a year is dropped for failing to progress, and many of them buy Chinese vials or copy pills by mail. Medicare still covers only hearts, kidneys, diabetes, sleep apnoea and a narrow dementia code, and it spends about forty billion dollars doing so.

The Pentagon made the drug part of readiness. The December defence bill turned the Army's recruit pilot into a three-service programme: recruits and soldiers over body-fat standards get a daily pill, a monthly adherence check and a fitness test. Around Fort Bragg it is unremarkable. The FAA cleared pilots to fly on it after a two-week observation period, and forty big police departments pay for officers to take it.

Then came the smell finding. In September 2035 a Danish and Veterans Affairs study reported that people on semaglutide or tirzepatide continuously for more than five years were more than twice as likely to lose their sense of smell. Most of the affected group is in their late fifties and sixties, the early adopters who started in 2021 and stayed on. Fewer than half got some back after a year off. In June the FDA told doctors to ask about it and told patients to check their smoke alarms. Firefighters' unions asked for screening. Flavour companies launched bolder soups.

The finding met a complaint that was already everywhere. 'The flats' is a household phrase, and a third of users say they stepped down a dose or took a planned break last year. Within weeks of the FDA notice, the largest employer adherence vendors began counting a clinician-documented pause of up to eight weeks as compliant, so the holiday became an administrative code. Musicians pause for tours and couples pause for anniversaries. Sportsbooks see a December bump. Deployed soldiers and police cadets are not allowed to pause at all.

An Ohio federal court ruled that promoting workers with complete adherence records is not disability discrimination, and the appeal is pending. Illinois is still the only state that bans adherence-tied premiums. Spirits volumes are down a fifth since 2025. The eleven state bans on prescribing to children under twelve stand, and no child who started early has yet reached final adult height.

Nothing in the country looks broken. A great many people are scheduling their eight weeks.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renata Salas burns the onions at 6:40 and does not know until Marcus, nineteen, waves a towel at the hospital kitchen hood.

"Chef. Smoke."

She has run the cafeteria line at Riverside for eleven years and has been on Wegovy for nine of them. Her employer track pays for the pen. She skipped it for one week in 2029 and got the premium letter. She tastes the chili and hands Marcus the spoon. He adds salt twice and she nods as if she agrees.

On break she sits in her car with the clinician form open on her phone. Reason for pause: Olfactory change, patient-reported. Requested duration: 8 weeks. The vendor app shows a green bar, 312 days adherent, and a small grey line under it: Pause allowance remaining: 56 days.

The nurse practitioner calls at 1:15. "Eight weeks probably won't tell us anything," she says. "But it might."

"And after eight?"

"Then you're non-compliant, and you know what that costs."

Her nephew Danny texts a photo from Fort Benning, a blister pack held up next to his face. Day 40. Down 11. Drill sgt says I'm a machine.

At home her husband, Luis, never on it, never needed it, is frying chorizo. She stands in the doorway and breathes in as hard as she can. There is something there, faint, like a radio in another room.

"You smell that?" he asks.

"Yeah," she says.

She signs the form at the kitchen table and puts the pen box at the back of the fridge, behind the eggs, where she will see it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: (~30,000 accessions a year on body-fat waivers, ~240,000 participants total), mostly on high-dose Foundayo
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: The program was created in Dec 2035 and high-dose Foundayo was approved only in Mar 2036. Yet 240,000 participants, mostly on that product, are asserted by year-end with no ramp or supply chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Persistence: one-year persistence on full-dose regimens rose from ~1/3 to ~40% with high-dose oral Foundayo and adherence-conditioned coverage.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: High-dose Foundayo had been on the market only about nine months, so it cannot explain a rise in measured one-year persistence. It is also unclear why persistence rises when holidays and cycling are said to be becoming the norm.

rationale.badness: Relative to the 2026 reference world (anchor 3), this world has 38% of adults on drug, adherence-conditioned employer and Medicaid coverage with ~18% annual disenrolment, and surveillance via smart caps and pause codes. It also has 18.5M gray-market users, a persistent smell-loss signal in 9–11M long-term users, a military readiness pill, and ~58% of users on repeat courses. Pervasive unmeasured low-dose anhedonia, class-sorted explanations for being 'off' (holiday at the top, lost track at the bottom) and weak epistemics on long-run harms make it a society many would refuse to live in. It is not catastrophic, and the 2033 counterfeit-insulin cluster did not recur.

rationale.badness: Compared with 2026 (11% on-drug, voluntary, weakly conditioned), this world has 38% of adults on-drug and adherence verified through smart caps and pause-code data sent to employers, Medicaid contractors and the military. The disenrolment of ~18% a year of Medicaid enrollees for 'non-progress' pushes people to gray vials, 18.5M people use gray product, and a new long-horizon smell-loss harm falls on 9–11M early adopters. Inequality is structural: holidays for the upper tier, 'lost my track' for the bottom. Epistemic and cohesion costs are moderate because the harms are named and discussed. Overall it is a recognisably harder society, not a refuse-to-live-in one.

Ever-used at 50.4 sits at the 50.8 ceiling, and pediatric 1.3% overall is a bit high against 12–17s at 3.0% and 6–11s at 0.11%, which implies about 1.07%.
